Plot a periodic table with a continuous value overlay

Source: R/ggPSE.R
ggPSE.Rd

The core plotting function of ggPSE. Returns a ggplot2 object that can be further modified.

Usage

ggPSE(
  data = NULL,
  value_col = NULL,
  symbol_col = "symbol",
  label_value = TRUE,
  value_digits = 2,
  color_low = "#fdf0f2",
  color_high = "#9a031e",
  color_na = "#f0f0f0",
  tile_border = NULL,
  highlight = NULL,
  legend_title = NULL,
  show_atomic_number = FALSE,
  base_size = 10,
  groups = NULL,
  periods = NULL,
  lanthanides = TRUE,
  actinides = TRUE,
  symbol_position = "center",
  number_position = "top-left",
  symbol_size = NULL,
  label_na = TRUE,
  text_color = NULL,
  symbol_nudge = 0,
  number_nudge = 0,
  highlight_colors = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the element symbols (case-sensitive, e.g. "Cl") and the value column. Rows may repeat for an element (e.g. one row per country) as long as they agree on the value; different values for the same element, unknown or NA symbols and non-numeric values give an error. If NULL, a blank table using the NA color is drawn.

value_col

Character. Column name in data to map to fill color.

symbol_col

Character. Column in data containing element symbols. Default "symbol".

label_value

Logical. Print numeric values inside tiles. Default TRUE.

value_digits

Integer. Decimal places for displayed values. Default 2.

color_low

Hex color for the low end of the gradient. Default "#fdf0f2".

color_high

Hex color for the high end of the gradient. Default "#9a031e".

color_na

Hex color for elements with no data. Default "#f0f0f0".

tile_border

Color for tile borders. If NULL (default) no border is drawn ("transparent"). Set a color such as "white" or "grey30" to draw borders.

highlight

Elements to colour by category. Either

  • a named list of symbol vectors, e.g. list("Alkali metals" = c("Li", "Na", "K"), Halogens = c("F", "Cl")). The names become the legend labels and the list order the legend order. split(df$symbol, df$category) gives such a list; use a factor for category to control the order. Colours come from highlight_colors.

  • or a list of groups, each a list with symbols (character vector of element symbols), color (fill color) and an optional label (legend label), e.g. list(list(symbols = c("Li","Co"), color = "#2166ac", label = "Battery metals")).

Unknown symbols and elements listed in more than one group give a warning (in that case the last group wins).

legend_title

Character. Legend title. Defaults to value_col; for highlight groups there is no title unless you set one.

show_atomic_number

Logical. Show atomic numbers inside the tile. Default FALSE. See number_position for where it is drawn.

base_size

Numeric. Base font size in pt. Default 10.

groups

Integer vector of length 2. Range of IUPAC groups (columns) to display, e.g. c(3, 12) for transition metals only. Default NULL shows all groups.

periods

Integer vector of length 2. Range of periods (rows 1-7) to display, e.g. c(4, 6) for periods 4 to 6. Default NULL shows all periods. Note: lanthanides and actinides are controlled separately via lanthanides and actinides.

lanthanides

Logical. Show the lanthanide row. Default TRUE.

actinides

Logical. Show the actinide row. Default TRUE.

symbol_position

Where the element symbol is drawn inside the tile: "center" (default), "top", "bottom", "left" or "right". If a value label is shown (label_value = TRUE), it is placed on the opposite side for "top" / "bottom", and stacked under the symbol for "left" / "right".

number_position

Where the atomic number is drawn when show_atomic_number = TRUE: "top-left" (default), "top", "top-right", "left", "right", "bottom-left", "bottom" or "bottom-right". A warning is given if it overlaps with the symbol or value text.

symbol_size

Size of the element symbol in ggplot2 text units (mm, as in the size argument of geom_text()). Default NULL scales with base_size (base_size * 0.4). Only the symbol is affected; the value and atomic number keep scaling with base_size. Large symbols need more room, see symbol_position.

label_na

Logical. Draw symbols (and atomic numbers / values) on tiles without data? Default TRUE. With FALSE, tiles that have no value (or are not part of a highlight group) stay blank, which is useful when only a subset of elements is covered by your data. Ignored when neither value_col nor highlight is given.

text_color

A single colour used for all tile text instead of the automatic black/white contrast colour. Default NULL. Useful when the fill scale is replaced afterwards (e.g. with scale_fill_gradient2()), because the automatic colour is derived from color_low / color_high.

symbol_nudge, number_nudge

Numeric. Vertical shift of the symbol / atomic number in tile units (a tile is 0.92 high; positive moves up), added to the position set by symbol_position / number_position. Default 0. The value label is not moved, and the overlap warning does not take the nudge into account.

highlight_colors

Colours for a named-list highlight: either a vector named by group (order does not matter, extra names are ignored) or an unnamed vector matched by position. Any R colour is accepted. Default NULL uses a colour-blind-safe palette (Okabe-Ito, extended beyond 8 groups). Ignored, with a warning, if the groups carry their own color.

Value

A ggplot object.

Examples

battery <- data.frame(
  symbol     = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe"),
  importance = c(0.95, 0.88, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45)
)
ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance", legend_title = "Battery relevance")


ggPSE(highlight = list(
  list(symbols = c("Li", "Co", "Ni"), color = "#2166ac", label = "Battery"),
  list(symbols = c("Nd", "Dy", "Tb"), color = "#e63946", label = "Magnets")
))


# Categories from a named list, with your own colours
ggPSE(highlight = list(Alkali = c("Li", "Na", "K"), Halogens = c("F", "Cl", "Br")),
      highlight_colors = c(Alkali = "firebrick", Halogens = "steelblue"),
      legend_title = "Group")


# Show only transition metals (groups 3-12, periods 4-6)
ggPSE(groups = c(3, 12), periods = c(4, 6), lanthanides = FALSE, actinides = FALSE)


# Symbol at the top, atomic number in the bottom-right corner
ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance",
      symbol_position = "top", show_atomic_number = TRUE,
      number_position = "bottom-right")
#> Warning: number_position = "bottom-right" overlaps with the symbol or value text when symbol_position = "top"; choose another number_position.


# Smaller symbols independent of base_size
ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance", symbol_size = 3)


# Only label the elements that have data, with one fixed text colour
ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance", label_na = FALSE, text_color = "grey15")


# Fine-tune: symbol slightly above its position
ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance", symbol_position = "top",
      symbol_nudge = 0.05)
